analysis:
Examined the docs updates, the GLM fixture README, the mlx-swift-lm submodule bump and the new GLM5NextWiredLimit.swift. No concrete security regression is supported by the supplied evidence.

1) docs/reference/protocol-messages.md (lines ~1144-1155) only documents the GLM reasoning-control and tool/JSON behavior. The documented behavior is validate-before-expose: forced tool_choice and JSON modes return 422 tool_noncompliance with nothing exposed on failure. Caller model names cannot select the path, and reserved schema metadata is rejected. Nothing in the wire contract or the trust grants changes. The source behind it (GLM5NextPromptPolicy, ToolChoiceEnforcementPolicy) is not in the supplied units, so I could not verify those claims.

2) fixtures/.../README.md only changes prose, and it explicitly says the vectors do not qualify these modes.

3) The libs/mlx-swift-lm submodule moves from 7bed821 to 6148b6d. The diff content is not supplied, so I cannot assess supply-chain or inference-engine changes. This touches TB-007 and the integrity of the native MLX engine, and it needs human or build-lane review of the submodule diff.

4) GLM5NextWiredLimit.swift is advisory only. It reads sysctls through sysctlbyname with fixed names, with no user-controlled input. It emits operator-copyable commands, including a LaunchDaemon plist built from numeric constants. It does not execute anything or write the plist itself. The plist and sysctl command are built from constants and numeric values, so there is no injection. The Metal OOM detection matches strings, and the notice carries no request content, so there is no prompt leakage (A-001). The remaining open question is whether callers (CLI doctor/restart) print or execute these commands unsafely. Those callers are not in this batch.

The prefix-cache sections (T-041) in the docs are unchanged in this diff.
